properties.description: Sync committee messages must be sent within the slot-relative timing window defined by get_sync_message_due_ms(epoch) using SYNC_MESSAGE_DUE_BPS. No valid sync message can be broadcast before slot start or after the computed due time.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ msg ∈ SyncCommitteeMessages: slot_start_time(msg.slot) ≤ msg.broadcast_time ≤ slot_start_time(msg.slot) + get_sync_message_due_ms(msg.epoch)
properties.attack_scenario: Attacker broadcasts sync committee messages far ahead of schedule to influence fork choice before honest validators process the block
properties.impact_if_violated: Fork choice manipulation through premature sync committee participation, potentially causing chain reorganizations

properties.description: The state transition from SLOT-START to SYNC-MESSAGE-DUE must involve computing the due time using the SYNC_MESSAGE_DUE_BPS configuration constant. The computation must be deterministic and identical across all nodes for the same epoch.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ epoch, ∀ node1, node2: get_sync_message_due_ms(epoch, node1) = get_sync_message_due_ms(epoch, node2)
properties.attack_scenario: Implementation inconsistencies in due time calculation cause network partitioning where different nodes have different timing expectations
properties.impact_if_violated: Network split where sync committee messages are rejected by some validators as mistimed

properties.description: Only validators currently in the sync committee for the target slot are authorized to broadcast sync committee messages. Messages from non-committee members must be rejected at the gossip layer.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ msg ∈ SyncCommitteeMessages: is_accepted(msg) ⟹ msg.validator_index ∈ get_sync_committee(state, compute_epoch_at_slot(msg.slot))
properties.attack_scenario: Attackers flood the network with fake sync committee messages from non-member validators to DoS the gossip layer
properties.impact_if_violated: Network congestion and potential eclipsing of legitimate sync committee messages

properties.description: The sync committee message must include a valid signature over the beacon block root at the attested slot. The signature must be verifiable using the validator's public key from the beacon state.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ msg ∈ SyncCommitteeMessages: bls_verify(pubkey=state.validators[msg.validator_index].pubkey, message=msg.beacon_block_root, signature=msg.signature) = true
properties.attack_scenario: Attacker creates sync committee messages with forged signatures to attest to malicious blocks
properties.impact_if_violated: Compromised fork choice allowing consensus on invalid blocks

properties.description: Sync committee contributions must be submitted within the slot-relative timing window defined by get_contribution_due_ms(epoch) using CONTRIBUTION_DUE_BPS. Contributions submitted outside this window must be rejected.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ contrib ∈ SyncContributions: slot_start_time(contrib.slot) ≤ contrib.submission_time ≤ slot_start_time(contrib.slot) + get_contribution_due_ms(contrib.epoch)
properties.attack_scenario: Late submission of contributions after block proposal deadline to cause fork choice inconsistencies
properties.impact_if_violated: Sync committee contributions arriving too late for block inclusion, reducing participation rate

properties.description: The transition from SYNC-MESSAGES-COLLECTED to CONTRIBUTION-SUBMITTED requires aggregation of individual messages before the contribution due time. The aggregation must include only valid, unique sync messages from distinct committee members.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ contrib ∈ SyncContributions: contrib.aggregation_bits.count() ≤ SYNC_COMMITTEE_SIZE ∧ ∀ bit_i, bit_j where i≠j: contrib.included_messages[i].validator_index ≠ contrib.included_messages[j].validator_index
properties.attack_scenario: Aggregator submits contribution with duplicate messages from the same validator inflating participation
properties.impact_if_violated: Double-counting of sync committee votes leading to incorrect fork choice weight calculations

properties.description: Only designated sync committee aggregators are authorized to submit aggregated contributions. Non-aggregators must not have their submissions accepted.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ contrib ∈ SyncContributions: is_accepted(contrib) ⟹ is_sync_committee_aggregator(state, contrib.slot, contrib.subcommittee_index, contrib.aggregator_index)
properties.attack_scenario: Non-aggregator validators submit contributions to flood the network or submit conflicting aggregations
properties.impact_if_violated: Network bandwidth exhaustion and potential eclipsing of legitimate contributions

properties.description: The aggregated sync committee contribution must contain a valid aggregate BLS signature over all included individual sync messages. The aggregation bits must accurately represent which validators are included.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ contrib ∈ SyncContributions: let pubkeys = [state.validators[i].pubkey for i in contrib.included_validators] in bls_aggregate_verify(pubkeys, contrib.beacon_block_root, contrib.signature) = true
properties.attack_scenario: Aggregator submits contribution with invalid aggregate signature or mismatched aggregation bits
properties.impact_if_violated: Invalid sync committee data propagated through the network, corrupting fork choice

properties.description: The maximum number of sync committee contributions per slot is bounded by the number of subcommittees (SYNC_COMMITTEE_SUBNET_COUNT). No more than one valid contribution per subcommittee per slot.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ slot: |{contrib ∈ SyncContributions : contrib.slot = slot}| ≤ SYNC_COMMITTEE_SUBNET_COUNT ∧ ∀ contrib1, contrib2 where contrib1.slot = contrib2.slot ∧ contrib1.subcommittee_index = contrib2.subcommittee_index: contrib1 = contrib2
properties.attack_scenario: Multiple conflicting contributions for the same subcommittee cause confusion in fork choice
properties.impact_if_violated: Ambiguity in which contribution should be included in blocks

properties.description: All consolidation requests in the queue must have passed format validation (source address 20 bytes, source pubkey 48 bytes, target pubkey 48 bytes) and fee validation (submitted ETH >= computed exponential fee). Invalid requests must never enter the queue.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ req ∈ ConsolidationQueue: (|req.source_address| = 20) ∧ (|req.source_pubkey| = 48) ∧ (|req.target_pubkey| = 48) ∧ (req.fee_paid ≥ compute_consolidation_fee(req.timestamp))
properties.attack_scenario: Malformed or underfunded consolidation requests bypass validation and enter the queue, causing system call failures
properties.impact_if_violated: Block invalidity due to failed system calls or processing of malformed consolidation data

properties.description: When a consolidation request is rejected due to insufficient fee, the state must transition to REQUEST-REJECTED-INSUFFICIENT-FEE and the fee must be refunded. No state changes to the consolidation queue occur.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ req: (req.fee_paid < compute_consolidation_fee(req.timestamp)) ⟹ (state_after = STATE-REQUEST-REJECTED-INSUFFICIENT-FEE) ∧ (queue_size_after = queue_size_before) ∧ (req.source_address.balance_after = req.source_address.balance_before + req.fee_paid)
properties.attack_scenario: System incorrectly accepts underfunded requests or fails to refund rejected requests
properties.impact_if_violated: Economic loss for users if fees are not refunded; queue pollution if invalid requests accepted

properties.description: When the consolidation queue exceeds the 262,144 capacity limit, new requests must transition to REQUEST-REJECTED-QUEUE-FULL state. The fee must NOT be refunded per EIP-7251 specification.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ req: (|ConsolidationQueue| ≥ 262144) ⟹ (state_after = STATE-REQUEST-REJECTED-QUEUE-FULL) ∧ (req.source_address.balance_after = req.source_address.balance_before - req.fee_paid) ∧ (queue_size_after = 262144)
properties.attack_scenario: Attacker fills the 262,144 queue with their own requests, causing legitimate requests to be discarded without refund (economic DoS)
properties.impact_if_violated: Loss of user funds if fees are incorrectly refunded; queue overflow if limit not enforced

properties.description: The consolidation request queue size must never exceed 262,144 entries. This is a hard protocol limit enforced at the EL predeploy contract level.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ block, ∀ state: |ConsolidationQueue(state)| ≤ 262144
properties.attack_scenario: Queue overflow leading to unbounded memory consumption or integer overflow in queue indexing
properties.impact_if_violated: Denial of service through memory exhaustion; potential consensus failures

properties.description: The computed consolidation fee must monotonically increase as the excess request count increases, per the exponential formula fake_exponential(MIN_FEE, excess, UPDATE_FRACTION). The fee must equal MIN_FEE when excess is zero.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ excess1, excess2: (excess1 < excess2) ⟹ (compute_consolidation_fee(excess1) < compute_consolidation_fee(excess2)) ∧ (compute_consolidation_fee(0) = MIN_CONSOLIDATION_REQUEST_FEE)
properties.attack_scenario: Fee calculation errors allow attackers to spam consolidation requests at artificially low prices
properties.impact_if_violated: Fee market failure enabling queue DoS attacks

properties.description: The consolidation system call must be invoked exactly once per block at the end of transaction execution, with exactly 30M gas limit, from SYSTEM_ADDRESS. The call must not be included in user-accessible transaction gas accounting.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ block: (system_call_count = 1) ∧ (system_call.gas_limit = 30_000_000) ∧ (system_call.caller = SYSTEM_ADDRESS) ∧ (system_call.gas_used ∉ block.gas_used)
properties.attack_scenario: Missing or duplicate system call invocations cause consolidation queue to stall or double-process
properties.impact_if_violated: Consolidation requests not processed or processed multiple times; block invalidity

properties.description: If no code exists at the consolidation predeploy address (0x0000BBdDc7CE488642fb579F8B00f3a590007251), the block must transition to NO-CODE-PRESENT state and become invalid. The block must be rejected by all validators.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ block: (code_length(0x0000BBdDc7CE488642fb579F8B00f3a590007251) = 0) ⟹ (block.valid = false) ∧ (state_after = STATE-NO-CODE-PRESENT)
properties.attack_scenario: Predeploy contract missing after chain upgrade, causing all blocks to fail
properties.impact_if_violated: Chain halts if predeploy is missing; consensus failure

properties.description: If the consolidation system call fails for any reason during execution, the block must transition to SYSTEM-CALL-FAILED state and become invalid. The state changes from the system call must be reverted.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ block: (system_call.success = false) ⟹ (block.valid = false) ∧ (state_after = state_before_system_call) ∧ (state = STATE-SYSTEM-CALL-FAILED)
properties.attack_scenario: Malicious contract code at predeploy address causes system call failures to halt the chain
properties.impact_if_violated: Blocks incorrectly accepted with failed system calls; state inconsistency

properties.description: The consolidation system call must process at most MAX_CONSOLIDATION_REQUESTS_PER_BLOCK (2) requests per block. Processing more than 2 requests violates the protocol limit.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ block: |processed_consolidations(block)| ≤ MAX_CONSOLIDATION_REQUESTS_PER_BLOCK ∧ MAX_CONSOLIDATION_REQUESTS_PER_BLOCK = 2
properties.attack_scenario: Implementation error processes more than 2 requests per block, causing state divergence between clients
properties.impact_if_violated: Consensus failure due to different processing rates across clients

properties.description: A validator's effective balance must never exceed MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_ELECTRA (2048 ETH) regardless of actual balance. Validators below MIN_ACTIVATION_BALANCE (32 ETH) must have effective balance of 0.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ validator: (validator.balance < MIN_ACTIVATION_BALANCE ⟹ validator.effective_balance = 0) ∧ (validator.effective_balance ≤ MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_ELECTRA) ∧ (MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_ELECTRA = 2048 ETH)
properties.attack_scenario: Implementation allows effective balance above 2048 ETH, giving validators disproportionate voting power
properties.impact_if_violated: Stake weight miscalculation leading to incorrect committee assignments and fork choice

properties.description: When a validator has the COMPOUNDING_WITHDRAWAL_PREFIX (0x02) credentials, their effective balance can range from 32 ETH to 2048 ETH based on actual balance. Without 0x02 prefix, effective balance is capped at 32 ETH in standard rewards mode.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ validator: (validator.withdrawal_credentials[0:1] = 0x02) ⟹ (32 ETH ≤ validator.effective_balance ≤ min(validator.balance, 2048 ETH)) ∧ (validator.withdrawal_credentials[0:1] ≠ 0x02) ⟹ (validator.effective_balance ≤ 32 ETH)
properties.attack_scenario: Validators with standard credentials incorrectly assigned >32 ETH effective balance, breaking protocol invariants
properties.impact_if_violated: Incorrect validator rewards and voting power distribution

properties.description: The effective balance computation must be deterministic and produce identical results across all nodes for the same validator balance and withdrawal credentials. The calculation must use integer arithmetic to avoid floating point inconsistencies.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ validator, ∀ node1, node2: compute_effective_balance(validator, node1) = compute_effective_balance(validator, node2)
properties.attack_scenario: Non-deterministic effective balance calculation causes consensus split between clients
properties.impact_if_violated: Network partition due to disagreement on validator effective balances

properties.description: The total effective balance weight of validator exits processed in a single epoch must not exceed the epoch churn limit (initially 256 ETH). Excess exit weight must be deferred to future epochs.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ epoch: sum(validator.effective_balance for validator in exits_processed(epoch)) ≤ get_epoch_churn_limit(epoch) ∧ initial_churn_limit = 256 ETH
properties.attack_scenario: Large validators (2048 ETH) exit simultaneously to rapidly deplete active stake and destabilize consensus
properties.impact_if_violated: Unstable validator set with rapid stake changes compromising security

properties.description: When an exit request exceeds the remaining churn limit for the epoch, the system must transition to EXIT-DEFERRED state and the partial exit mechanism must activate. The portion fitting within the churn limit is processed immediately, with the remainder queued.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ exit_request: (exit_request.effective_balance > remaining_churn(epoch)) ⟹ (process_weight = remaining_churn(epoch)) ∧ (deferred_weight = exit_request.effective_balance - remaining_churn(epoch)) ∧ (state = STATE-EXIT-DEFERRED)
properties.attack_scenario: Large exit requests bypass churn limiting by processing entire weight immediately instead of deferring
properties.impact_if_violated: Churn limit violated leading to rapid validator set changes

properties.description: The churn limit must scale with the total active validator balance according to the protocol formula. The limit must never fall below the minimum churn (256 ETH) regardless of total stake.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ epoch: get_epoch_churn_limit(epoch) = max(MIN_CHURN_LIMIT, total_active_balance(epoch) / CHURN_LIMIT_QUOTIENT) ∧ MIN_CHURN_LIMIT = 256 ETH
properties.attack_scenario: Churn limit calculation errors allow unbounded exit rates or set limit too low blocking exits
properties.impact_if_violated: Either validator set instability or validator exit queue gridlock

properties.description: The consolidation fee must dynamically adjust based on excess requests using the exponential formula fake_exponential(MIN_FEE, excess, UPDATE_FRACTION). The fee must equal MIN_CONSOLIDATION_REQUEST_FEE (1 wei) when excess is zero.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ state: (excess_requests(state) = 0 ⟹ consolidation_fee(state) = 1 wei) ∧ (excess_requests(state) > 0 ⟹ consolidation_fee(state) > 1 wei) ∧ consolidation_fee(state) = fake_exponential(1, excess_requests(state), UPDATE_FRACTION)
properties.attack_scenario: Fee remains at 1 wei regardless of demand, enabling queue spam without economic cost
properties.impact_if_violated: Queue DoS via cheap consolidation requests flooding the system

properties.description: When actual requests per block exceed the target, the excess counter must increase and the fee must transition to FEE-INCREASED state with exponentially higher base fee. When below target, excess decreases and fee transitions to FEE-DECREASED state.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ block: (requests_in_block > target_requests ⟹ excess_after > excess_before ∧ fee_after > fee_before ∧ state = STATE-FEE-INCREASED) ∧ (requests_in_block < target_requests ⟹ excess_after < excess_before ∧ fee_after < fee_before ∧ state = STATE-FEE-DECREASED)
properties.attack_scenario: Fee adjustment mechanism fails, allowing sustained spam even when demand is high
properties.impact_if_violated: Economic DoS on consolidation system

properties.description: The excess request counter must accurately track the cumulative difference between actual and target requests per block over time. The counter must never become negative (minimum 0).
properties.formal_statement: ∀ block: excess_requests(block) = max(0, excess_requests(block-1) + requests_in_block(block-1) - target_requests_per_block) ∧ excess_requests(genesis) = 0
properties.attack_scenario: Integer underflow or overflow in excess counter corrupts fee calculation
properties.impact_if_violated: Incorrect consolidation fees, potential fee market manipulation

properties.description: All transactions must have a valid type byte that is either in the typed transaction range [0x00-0x7f] or the legacy RLP range [0xc0-0xfe]. Bytes in the undefined range [0x80-0xbf] or reserved byte 0xff must cause transaction rejection.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx: is_valid(tx) ⟹ (tx.first_byte ∈ [0x00..0x7f] ∨ tx.first_byte ∈ [0xc0..0xfe]) ∧ (tx.first_byte ∉ [0x80..0xbf] ∧ tx.first_byte ≠ 0xff)
properties.attack_scenario: Malformed transactions with invalid type bytes bypass validation and corrupt mempool or block processing
properties.impact_if_violated: Consensus failures due to invalid transactions in blocks

properties.description: When a transaction type byte is recognized as a typed transaction (0x00-0x7f), validation must confirm the type is currently activated and known. Unrecognized or future types must cause transition to TX-TYPE-ERROR state.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx: (tx.first_byte ∈ [0x00..0x7f]) ⟹ (tx.type ∈ {0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03} ⟹ state = STATE-TX-TYPE-VALID) ∧ (tx.type ∉ {0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03} ⟹ state = STATE-TX-TYPE-ERROR)
properties.attack_scenario: Future transaction types accepted prematurely before fork activation
properties.impact_if_violated: Consensus split between nodes with different supported transaction types

properties.description: Contract creation transactions must only be accepted for transaction types that explicitly permit it. Type 3 (blob) transactions attempting contract creation must transition to CONTRACT-CREATION-ERROR state.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx: (tx.to = null ∧ tx.type = 0x03) ⟹ (state = STATE-CONTRACT-CREATION-ERROR) ∧ (tx.to = null ∧ tx.type ∈ {0x00, 0x01, 0x02}) ⟹ (contract_creation_allowed = true)
properties.attack_scenario: Blob transactions used to create contracts, violating EIP-4844 design constraints
properties.impact_if_violated: Protocol violation allowing unintended contract deployments via blob transactions

properties.description: For EIP-1559 transactions, max_fee_per_gas must be greater than or equal to the block base fee. Transactions with max_fee below base fee must transition to INSUFFICIENT-MAX-FEE state and be rejected.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx ∈ EIP1559Transactions: is_accepted(tx) ⟹ tx.max_fee_per_gas ≥ block.base_fee_per_gas
properties.attack_scenario: Transactions with insufficient max_fee accepted into blocks, violating EIP-1559 economics
properties.impact_if_violated: Block invalidity due to transactions that cannot pay required base fee

properties.description: The max_priority_fee_per_gas must never exceed max_fee_per_gas. Transactions violating this constraint must transition to PRIORITY-FEE-ERROR state and be rejected.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx ∈ EIP1559Transactions: is_accepted(tx) ⟹ tx.max_priority_fee_per_gas ≤ tx.max_fee_per_gas
properties.attack_scenario: Malformed transactions with priority fee > max fee bypass validation
properties.impact_if_violated: Fee calculation errors leading to incorrect miner payments or transaction rejection

properties.description: The effective priority fee paid to the miner must be min(max_priority_fee_per_gas, max_fee_per_gas - base_fee_per_gas). This ensures the user never pays more than their specified maximum.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx ∈ EIP1559Transactions: effective_priority_fee(tx) = min(tx.max_priority_fee_per_gas, tx.max_fee_per_gas - block.base_fee_per_gas) ∧ effective_priority_fee(tx) ≥ 0
properties.attack_scenario: Fee calculation errors cause users to overpay or miners to receive incorrect fees
properties.impact_if_violated: Economic loss for users; incorrect block rewards for miners

properties.description: Blob transactions must not exceed the protocol blob gas limit. The total blob gas for a transaction must be calculated as blob_count * GAS_PER_BLOB and must not exceed MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_TRANSACTION.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx ∈ BlobTransactions: tx.blob_gas = |tx.blob_versioned_hashes| * GAS_PER_BLOB ∧ tx.blob_gas ≤ MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_TRANSACTION
properties.attack_scenario: Transactions with excessive blob count bypass gas limits, causing block size explosion
properties.impact_if_violated: Network bandwidth exhaustion and storage bloat from oversized blob transactions

properties.description: The max_fee_per_blob_gas in a blob transaction must be greater than or equal to the current blob base fee. Transactions with insufficient blob fee must transition to INSUFFICIENT-BLOB-FEE state.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx ∈ BlobTransactions: is_accepted(tx) ⟹ tx.max_fee_per_blob_gas ≥ block.blob_base_fee
properties.attack_scenario: Blob transactions with insufficient fee accepted, violating EIP-4844 fee market
properties.impact_if_violated: Block invalidity or economic DoS on blob storage

properties.description: Each blob_versioned_hash must have the correct format: version byte prefix (0x01) followed by 31 bytes of KZG commitment hash. The hash must correspond to a valid KZG commitment for the blob data.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ hash ∈ tx.blob_versioned_hashes: (hash[0] = 0x01) ∧ (|hash| = 32) ∧ (hash[1:32] = sha256(kzg_commitment)[0:31]) ∧ verify_blob_kzg_proof(blob, kzg_commitment, kzg_proof) = true
properties.attack_scenario: Invalid versioned hashes accepted, allowing blob data to be omitted or corrupted
properties.impact_if_violated: Data availability failure — blobs referenced but not actually available

properties.description: A blob transaction with blob_versioned_hashes but no actual blob data must transition to NO-BLOB-DATA state and be rejected. The transaction must include actual blob content matching all versioned hashes.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx ∈ BlobTransactions: (|tx.blob_versioned_hashes| > 0 ∧ |tx.blobs| = 0) ⟹ (state = STATE-NO-BLOB-DATA) ∧ (is_accepted = false)
properties.attack_scenario: Transactions claim blobs but provide no data, passing validation incorrectly
properties.impact_if_violated: Blob transactions accepted without actual blob data, breaking data availability guarantees

properties.description: The number of blobs per transaction must be bounded by MAX_BLOBS_PER_TRANSACTION. The number of blob_versioned_hashes must exactly match the number of provided blobs.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx ∈ BlobTransactions: |tx.blob_versioned_hashes| ≤ MAX_BLOBS_PER_TRANSACTION ∧ |tx.blob_versioned_hashes| = |tx.blobs|
properties.attack_scenario: Mismatch between blob hashes and actual blobs causes validation inconsistencies
properties.impact_if_violated: Data integrity violations with unverifiable blob references

properties.description: Contract creation transactions must have init code size not exceeding MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE. Transactions with oversized init code must transition to INIT-CODE-TOO-LARGE state and be rejected.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx: (tx.to = null) ⟹ (|tx.data| ≤ MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE ∨ state = STATE-INIT-CODE-TOO-LARGE)
properties.attack_scenario: Massive init code transactions bypass size limits, causing DoS during contract creation
properties.impact_if_violated: Denial of service via memory exhaustion during contract deployment

properties.description: The CREATE2 deterministic address must be computed as keccak256(0xff ++ sender_address ++ salt ++ keccak256(init_code))[12:]. The same inputs must always produce the same address across all nodes.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ sender, salt, init_code, ∀ node1, node2: compute_create2_address(sender, salt, init_code, node1) = compute_create2_address(sender, salt, init_code, node2) = keccak256(0xff ++ sender ++ salt ++ keccak256(init_code))[12:]
properties.attack_scenario: Non-deterministic address calculation causes different nodes to deploy contracts to different addresses
properties.impact_if_violated: Consensus failure with contracts deployed to different addresses on different nodes

properties.description: When the computed CREATE2 address already contains code or has nonzero nonce, the operation must transition to COLLISION-DETECTED state and then to CREATE2-FAILED state. No contract deployment occurs and zero is pushed to the stack.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ create2_op: ((code_length(create2_op.address) > 0) ∨ (nonce(create2_op.address) > 0)) ⟹ (state = STATE-COLLISION-DETECTED) ⟹ (state = STATE-CREATE2-FAILED) ∧ (stack.top = 0)
properties.attack_scenario: Front-running attack: attacker deploys contract at predicted CREATE2 address before legitimate deployer
properties.impact_if_violated: Address collision allows attacker to squat on predicted addresses

properties.description: When no address collision exists, CREATE2 must transition through EXECUTE-INIT state where init code runs. On success, transitions to CONTRACT-DEPLOYED state with the new contract address on stack. On failure, transitions to CREATE2-FAILED with zero on stack.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ create2_op: (no_collision(create2_op.address)) ⟹ (execute_init_code(create2_op.init_code, create2_op.endowment) ⟹ (state = STATE-CONTRACT-DEPLOYED ∧ stack.top = create2_op.address) ∨ (state = STATE-CREATE2-FAILED ∧ stack.top = 0))
properties.attack_scenario: Init code execution failure not properly handled, leaving inconsistent state
properties.impact_if_violated: Partially deployed contracts or incorrect return values from CREATE2

properties.description: CREATE2 must charge base CREATE cost (32000 gas) plus init code hash cost (6 gas per 32-byte word) plus memory expansion cost. Total gas must be deducted before execution begins.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ create2_op: gas_cost(create2_op) = 32000 + (6 * ceil(|init_code| / 32)) + memory_expansion_cost(memory_start, memory_length) ∧ (available_gas < gas_cost ⟹ state = STATE-INSUFFICIENT-GAS)
properties.attack_scenario: Gas calculation errors allow CREATE2 operations with insufficient gas, causing unexpected OOG failures mid-execution
properties.impact_if_violated: Inconsistent gas accounting; potential for DoS via underpriced CREATE2 operations

properties.description: Address collision check must verify both nonce == 0 and code_length == 0 per EIP-684. Any address with nonzero nonce OR existing code must cause CREATE2 to fail.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ address: is_available_for_create2(address) ⟺ (nonce(address) = 0 ∧ code_length(address) = 0)
properties.attack_scenario: Incomplete collision check allows deployment over existing accounts, enabling address squatting or contract replacement
properties.impact_if_violated: Security critical: allows overwriting existing contracts or account state

properties.description: The 0xff prefix byte in the CREATE2 address computation must be included as a raw byte (not RLP encoded) to ensure domain separation from CREATE addresses. This prevents cross-deployment address collisions.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ create2_op: address_preimage(create2_op) = bytes.concat(0xff, sender_address, salt, keccak256(init_code)) ∧ 0xff is not RLP encoded
properties.attack_scenario: Incorrect 0xff encoding allows finding CREATE and CREATE2 operations that produce the same address
properties.impact_if_violated: Address space collision between CREATE and CREATE2, enabling contract replacement attacks

properties.description: An EIP can only transition from DRAFT to ELIGIBLE-FOR-INCLUSION after successful presentation at AllCoreDevs and achievement of rough consensus. Without ACD approval, EIPs must remain in DRAFT state.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ eip: (state(eip) = DRAFT ∧ state_next(eip) = ELIGIBLE-FOR-INCLUSION) ⟹ (presented_at_acd(eip) = true ∧ rough_consensus_achieved(eip) = true)
properties.attack_scenario: N/A - governance process, not runtime security
properties.impact_if_violated: Governance failure: EIPs bypass community review process

properties.description: EIP eligibility validation requires three conditions: (1) conceptual support from core devs, (2) client teams willing to accept implementation PRs, (3) link to ACD meeting notes. Missing any condition transitions to VALIDATION-FAILED.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ eip: (state(eip) = FULLY-VALIDATED) ⟹ (conceptual_support(eip) = true ∧ implementation_acceptable(eip) = true ∧ has_acd_link(eip) = true)
properties.attack_scenario: N/A - governance process, not runtime security
properties.impact_if_violated: Governance failure: insufficiently reviewed EIPs advance to implementation

properties.description: When a wallet receives a Type 1 (EIP-2930) transaction for signing, it must automatically convert it to Type 2 (EIP-1559) by changing type from 0x1 to 0x2, removing gas_price, and creating max_fee_per_gas and max_priority_fee_per_gas fields. The access_list must be preserved unchanged.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx_type1: convert_to_type2(tx_type1) ⟹ (tx_type2.type = 0x2 ∧ tx_type2.max_fee_per_gas = tx_type1.gas_price ∧ tx_type2.max_priority_fee_per_gas = tx_type1.gas_price ∧ tx_type2.access_list = tx_type1.access_list ∧ 'gas_price' ∉ tx_type2)
properties.attack_scenario: Incorrect conversion corrupts transaction semantics or economics (e.g., wrong fee values)
properties.impact_if_violated: User transactions executed with unintended fee structure or missing access list

properties.description: The gas_price from Type 1 transaction must be mapped to BOTH max_fee_per_gas and max_priority_fee_per_gas in the Type 2 transaction, preserving user's maximum willingness to pay while enabling EIP-1559 refund benefits.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx_type1: (tx_type2 = convert(tx_type1)) ⟹ (tx_type2.max_fee_per_gas = tx_type1.gas_price ∧ tx_type2.max_priority_fee_per_gas = tx_type1.gas_price)
properties.attack_scenario: Incorrect fee mapping causes user to overpay (if max_fee set too high) or transaction to fail (if set too low)
properties.impact_if_violated: Economic loss for users; unexpected transaction failures

properties.description: RLPx auth packets must be encrypted using ECIES with the recipient's static public key. Only the intended recipient with the corresponding private key can decrypt the auth packet. Required fields (signature, initiator-pubk, initiator-nonce) must be present after decryption.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ auth_packet: can_decrypt(auth_packet, recipient_privkey) ⟺ auth_packet.encrypted_with = recipient_pubkey ∧ decrypted_auth_packet.has_fields(signature, initiator_pubk, initiator_nonce)
properties.attack_scenario: Man-in-the-middle intercepts and decrypts auth packets or forges packets without recipient's private key
properties.impact_if_violated: Connection hijacking or eavesdropping on P2P communications

properties.description: EIP-8 mandates forward-compatible parsing: version mismatches, additional RLP list elements, and trailing data in auth/ack packets must be ignored. Parsing must extract required fields and succeed even with unknown future extensions.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ auth_packet: (auth_packet.version ≠ current_version ∨ |auth_packet.rlp_list| > expected_elements ∨ |auth_packet.trailing_data| > 0) ⟹ (parse_tolerant(auth_packet) = success ∧ extract_required_fields(auth_packet) = success)
properties.attack_scenario: Malicious peers send malformed packets with extra data to exploit buffer overflows or cause crashes
properties.impact_if_violated: Denial of service via parser crashes; network instability

properties.description: Auth packet padding (100-300 bytes random) must use cryptographically secure random data to prevent traffic analysis. Predictable padding patterns could leak information about peer identity or network topology.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ auth_packet: (|auth_packet.padding| ∈ [100..300]) ∧ is_cryptographically_random(auth_packet.padding) = true
properties.attack_scenario: Traffic analysis using padding patterns to identify nodes or estimate network graph
properties.impact_if_violated: Privacy leak: network topology or node identities exposed through traffic analysis

properties.description: devp2p Hello packets must be parsed with forward-compatible tolerance per Postel's Law. Version mismatches and additional list elements must be ignored. Connections must succeed despite version differences as long as required fields are present.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ hello_packet: (hello_packet.version ≠ local_version) ⟹ (parse_hello(hello_packet) = success ∧ connection_established = true)
properties.attack_scenario: N/A - forward compatibility feature
properties.impact_if_violated: Network partitioning when nodes with different protocol versions cannot connect

properties.description: UDP discovery packets must not exceed 1280 bytes maximum size. Packets exceeding this limit must be rejected to prevent UDP fragmentation attacks.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ discovery_packet: |discovery_packet| ≤ 1280 ∨ is_rejected(discovery_packet) = true
properties.attack_scenario: Attackers send oversized UDP packets causing fragmentation-based amplification DoS
properties.impact_if_violated: Network bandwidth exhaustion via UDP fragmentation attacks

properties.description: Unknown discovery packet types must be silently discarded without error propagation. This enables forward compatibility with future discovery protocol extensions.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ discovery_packet: (discovery_packet.type ∉ {ping, pong, findnode, neighbours}) ⟹ (action = SILENT-DISCARD ∧ no_error_logged_to_peer)
properties.attack_scenario: N/A - forward compatibility feature
properties.impact_if_violated: Discovery protocol cannot evolve without hard forks

properties.description: EIP-8 validation intentionally skips version number checks. Only required fields (signature, nonces, public keys) are validated. Extra RLP elements and trailing data are ignored. Missing required fields cause validation failure.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ packet: (validation_result = PASSED) ⟺ (has_required_fields(packet) = true) ∧ version_check_skipped ∧ extra_elements_ignored
properties.attack_scenario: Malicious peers exploit tolerant parsing by including malformed extra data to trigger buffer overflows
properties.impact_if_violated: Security vulnerability: buffer overflows or crashes from malformed extra data

properties.description: Permission requests must only be granted after explicit user approval via consent prompt. The wallet must correctly identify the invoker (dApp origin) and prevent origin spoofing. Permissions granted without user consent violate the security model.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ permission_request: (permission_granted(permission_request) = true) ⟹ (user_approved(permission_request) = true ∧ invoker_verified(permission_request.invoker) = true)
properties.attack_scenario: Malicious dApp spoofs origin to inherit permissions from trusted dApp, bypassing user consent
properties.impact_if_violated: Privilege escalation: malicious dApps gain unauthorized access to wallet methods

properties.description: When user rejects a permission request, the wallet must transition to USER-REJECTED state, throw JSON-RPC error 4001 per EIP-1193, and not store any permission. No wallet state changes occur.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ permission_request: (user_decision = REJECT) ⟹ (state = STATE-USER-REJECTED ∧ error_code = 4001 ∧ permissions_unchanged)
properties.attack_scenario: Wallet incorrectly grants permissions despite user rejection
properties.impact_if_violated: Users lose control over permission grants; unauthorized dApp access

properties.description: Restricted wallet methods must only execute if a valid permission exists for the invoker with matching parentCapability AND all caveat constraints are satisfied. Unrestricted methods execute without permission checks.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ method_call: (is_restricted(method_call.method) ∧ executed(method_call) = true) ⟹ (∃ permission: permission.invoker = method_call.invoker ∧ permission.parentCapability = method_call.method ∧ satisfy_caveats(permission.caveats, method_call) = true)
properties.attack_scenario: dApp bypasses permission checks to execute restricted methods without consent
properties.impact_if_violated: Complete permission system bypass; unauthorized wallet access

properties.description: When a restricted method is called without a matching permission, the system must transition to PERMISSION-NOT-FOUND then METHOD-DENIED states. The method must not execute and an error must be returned.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ method_call: (is_restricted(method_call.method) ∧ ¬∃ permission: permission.invoker = method_call.invoker ∧ permission.parentCapability = method_call.method) ⟹ (state = STATE-PERMISSION-NOT-FOUND ⟹ state = STATE-METHOD-DENIED ∧ executed = false)
properties.attack_scenario: Method execution proceeds despite missing permission
properties.impact_if_violated: Authorization bypass allowing unpermissioned method calls

properties.description: When a valid permission exists but caveat validation fails, the system must transition to METHOD-DENIED state. Caveats provide fine-grained restrictions (e.g., allowed accounts) that must be enforced.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ method_call, permission: (permission.invoker = method_call.invoker ∧ satisfy_caveats(permission.caveats, method_call) = false) ⟹ (state = STATE-METHOD-DENIED ∧ executed = false)
properties.attack_scenario: dApp with permission accesses accounts or methods outside caveat restrictions
properties.impact_if_violated: Caveat bypass allowing over-permissioned access beyond granted scope

properties.description: wallet_getPermissions must filter the permission array to return only permissions where the invoker matches the calling origin. Permissions from other origins must not be leaked.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ invoker: permissions_returned(invoker) = {p ∈ permissions_store : p.invoker = invoker}
properties.attack_scenario: Information leak: dApp queries permissions of other origins to discover what capabilities they have
properties.impact_if_violated: Privacy violation exposing permission grants to unauthorized parties

properties.description: URLs in permission requests must be validated against SSRF attack vectors. Only whitelisted URL schemes (http, https) and ports must be allowed. Schemes like file://, gopher://, or non-standard ports accessing internal services must be blocked.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ url ∈ permission_request.urls: (url.scheme ∈ {http, https}) ∧ (url.port ∈ ALLOWED_PORTS) ∨ is_rejected(url) = true
properties.attack_scenario: Malicious dApp requests permission with file:/// URL to read local files or gopher:// to access internal services
properties.impact_if_violated: SSRF vulnerability allowing wallet to be used as proxy to attack internal network or file system

properties.description: Transaction type detection must correctly classify all transactions: first byte in [0x00-0x7f] is typed transaction, [0xc0-0xfe] is legacy RLP. Bytes in [0x80-0xbf] or 0xff are invalid and must cause rejection.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx: (tx.first_byte ∈ [0x00..0x7f] ⟹ tx.format = TYPED) ∧ (tx.first_byte ∈ [0xc0..0xfe] ⟹ tx.format = LEGACY) ∧ (tx.first_byte ∈ [0x80..0xbf] ∨ tx.first_byte = 0xff ⟹ is_rejected(tx) = true)
properties.attack_scenario: Malformed transactions with invalid type bytes bypass validation and corrupt mempool
properties.impact_if_violated: Transaction processing failures; consensus issues if invalid transactions enter blocks

properties.description: After extracting transaction type byte, validation must confirm the type is registered and activated for the current block height. Unrecognized or future types must transition to TYPE-INVALID state and be rejected.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx: (tx.type ∈ registered_types(block_height)) ⟹ (state = STATE-TYPE-VALID) ∧ (tx.type ∉ registered_types(block_height)) ⟹ (state = STATE-TYPE-INVALID ∧ is_rejected(tx) = true)
properties.attack_scenario: Future transaction types accepted before fork activation, causing consensus split
properties.impact_if_violated: Consensus failure: nodes disagree on valid transaction types for a block

properties.description: Transaction signing data MUST include the TransactionType byte as the first byte to ensure domain separation. Signatures created without the type byte are vulnerable to cross-type replay attacks. Verification must reject signatures where type byte is missing or mismatched.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx: signing_data(tx) = bytes.concat(tx.type, rlp_encode(tx.payload)) ∧ verify_signature(tx) ⟹ (tx.signature.signed_data[0] = tx.type)
properties.attack_scenario: Attacker reuses signature from Type 1 transaction to execute as Type 2 with different semantics
properties.impact_if_violated: Signature replay attack: transactions executed with unintended type and semantics

properties.description: Transaction receipts must be encoded in the same typed format as their transactions: TransactionType || ReceiptPayload. The receipt type must match the transaction type. Receipts are included in the receipt trie with this encoding.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ tx, receipt: (receipt.type = tx.type) ∧ encoded_receipt = bytes.concat(receipt.type, rlp_encode(receipt.payload)) ∧ receipt_trie_contains(encoded_receipt)
properties.attack_scenario: Receipt type mismatch causes merkle proof verification failures for transaction receipts
properties.impact_if_violated: Light client failures: cannot verify transaction inclusion or execution status

properties.description: Opcode mnemonic renaming must maintain exact hex value mappings: KECCAK256=0x20, EXTBALANCE=0x31, BLOCKNUMBER=0x43, BLOCKGASLIMIT=0x45, GASLEFT=0x5a, ABORT=0xfe. Assemblers must resolve mnemonics to identical opcodes regardless of naming.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ mnemonic: (resolve_mnemonic(KECCAK256) = 0x20) ∧ (resolve_mnemonic(EXTBALANCE) = 0x31) ∧ (resolve_mnemonic(BLOCKNUMBER) = 0x43) ∧ (resolve_mnemonic(BLOCKGASLIMIT) = 0x45) ∧ (resolve_mnemonic(GASLEFT) = 0x5a) ∧ (resolve_mnemonic(ABORT) = 0xfe)
properties.attack_scenario: N/A - tooling consistency, not runtime security
properties.impact_if_violated: Tooling fragmentation: different assemblers produce different bytecode for same source

properties.description: EIP-1803 opcode renaming must not change any hex opcode values or execution semantics. All deployed bytecode remains valid and executes identically regardless of mnemonic names used during compilation.
properties.formal_statement: ∀ bytecode_before, bytecode_after_eip1803: (source_code_uses_old_names = true ∨ source_code_uses_new_names = true) ⟹ (bytecode_before = bytecode_after_eip1803 ∧ execution_semantics(bytecode_before) = execution_semantics(bytecode_after_eip1803))
properties.attack_scenario: N/A - backward compatibility is design requirement
properties.impact_if_violated: Existing contracts break if semantics change
